{"id":"ENT-1938","title":"CLI: emit outcome telemetry for entire search invocations (success, error class, result count, duration)","description":"## Why

The internal tester audit of agent transcripts (6,572 sessions across [entire.io](<http://entire.io>) / entiredb / entire-api) found that of the search sessions with no observed value, **88.5% failed to obtain a usable response at all** — 32 of 46 were auth/configuration failures, 11 were results never collected. Operational reliability, not retrieval quality, is the dominant failure mode.

We currently cannot see this class of failure in telemetry:

* `cli_command_executed` records that `entire search` ran (391 runs / 26 machines in the last 14 days) but carries no outcome, error class, result count, or duration.
* entireio/cli #2024 (`cli_commit_condensed`) answers the adoption question ("did the session search when it should have") but not "did the search work".
* These failures happen **client-side and never reach a server** — keyring/auth failures and the `ErrNoCellForJurisdiction` cell skip abort before or during the request. Server-side logging cannot catch them; the CLI is the only place they can be measured.

## What

Add outcome properties to the search invocation telemetry (extend `cli_command_executed` for the search commands, or a dedicated event if cleaner):

* `success` (bool)
* `error_class` — coarse enum, at minimum distinguishing: auth/keyring failure, jurisdiction/cell skip (`ErrNoCellForJurisdiction`), network/timeout, server error (5xx), other. Must separate the two "region" variants — the flag-gate 404 misclass (fixed in CLI v0.10.1) and the client-side cell skip are different failures.
* `result_count` (int) — zero-result searches are a distinct signal from failures.
* `duration_ms`

Covers `entire search` and `entire checkpoint search`.

## Constraints

* Content-free by construction: never send query text, result snippets, or repo names. Booleans, enums, counts, durations only (same bar as #2024).
* Gate on `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` and the opt-in telemetry setting before any work, matching the existing detached-child PostHog path.
* Error classes come from typed errors, not string-matching error messages.

## Explicitly out of scope

Relevance/quality telemetry (`search_id`, scores, rerank metrics, server query log) — that was PR <pull-request id="1b08f022-ffbe-4985-b38c-3d5fece15c83" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/review/add-search-id-explain-hints-and-search-relevance-telemetry-ent-1528-f1fd71e1e2cf">entireio/cli#1960</pull-request> / <issue id="804ceab6-6e3b-4dc9-9002-3a2e12696524" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1528/cli-search-click-tracking-rider-search-id-impression-log-explain-time">ENT-1528</issue>, closed deliberately. The audit shows quality was rarely the problem (4 of 52 no-value cases); revisit only after this dashboard shows the failure classes are solved.

- Prefer the simplest implementation that answers the product question; push complexity to the analytics layer.

**How to apply:** When adding CLI events, follow the existing `telemetry` package pattern (`Build*Payload` + `Track*`, settings gate at call site, `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`), keep properties flat and anonymous, and correlate events by `distinct_id` + time in PostHog instead of local state. 92	// spawnAnalyticsHook replaces the detached spawn when non-nil so tests can
93	// assert how many sends a call performs and what each carries. Production
94	// leaves it nil. execx.SpawnDetached itself no-ops under `go test`, so counting
95	// sends needs a seam here rather than a spy on the child.
96	//
97	//nolint:gochecknoglobals // test seam, set and restored by in-package tests.
98	var spawnAnalyticsHook func(payloadJSON string)
99	
100	// spawnDetachedAnalytics sends the payload from a detached `entire
101	// __send_analytics` child so the network call never blocks the CLI. The empty
102	// dir keeps the child out of the parent's working directory. payloadJSON is
103	// one event object or an array of them — see SendEvents.
104	func spawnDetachedAnalytics(payloadJSON string) {
105		if spawnAnalyticsHook != nil {
106			spawnAnalyticsHook(payloadJSON)
107			return
108		}
109		execx.SpawnDetached("", "__send_analytics", payloadJSON)
110	}

112	// maxDetachedPayloadBytes bounds the JSON handed to one child. The payload
113	// travels as an argv element and argv limits are per-platform and modest
114	// (macOS caps the whole vector near 256KB), so an oversized batch is split
115	// across children rather than risking a spawn that fails wholesale. Far above
116	// any realistic batch: one event payload runs a few hundred bytes.
117	const maxDetachedPayloadBytes = 96 * 1024
118	
119	// spawnDetachedAnalyticsBatch sends every payload using as few detached
120	// children as the size budget allows — normally exactly one.
121	//
122	// Nothing is dropped: a batch too large for one argv is split, so an unusually
123	// long backlog costs an extra process instead of lost events. Batching also
124	// means the child resolves the git version once per send rather than once per
125	// event.
126	func spawnDetachedAnalyticsBatch(payloads []*EventPayload) {
127		const (
128			bracketsBytes = 2 // "[" and "]"
129			commaBytes    = 1
130		)
131		batch := make([]json.RawMessage, 0, len(payloads))
132		size := bracketsBytes
133	
134		flush := func() {
135			if len(batch) == 0 {
136				return
137			}
138			if batchJSON, err := json.Marshal(batch); err == nil {
139				spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(batchJSON))
140			}
141			batch = batch[:0]
142			size = bracketsBytes
143		}
144	
145		for _, payload := range payloads {
146			if payload == nil {
147				continue
148			}
149			payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
150			if err != nil {
151				continue
152			}
153			// Flush before appending so the batch stays within budget. A single
154			// payload over the budget still goes out alone: dropping it would be
155			// the silent loss this batching exists to remove.
156			if len(batch) > 0 && size+len(payloadJSON)+commaBytes > maxDetachedPayloadBytes {
157				flush()
158			}
159			batch = append(batch, payloadJSON)
160			size += len(payloadJSON) + commaBytes
161		}
162		flush()
163	}

326	// CommitCondensedSignal is the content-free adoption signal emitted when a
327	// commit condenses a session checkpoint: whether the session consulted entire
328	// search, and whether the committed files already carried AI checkpoint
329	// history. Together these give the "sessions that edited history-dense files
330	// without searching" denominator that raw command counts cannot. Content-free
331	// metadata only — booleans, a count, and the agent identifier; never file
332	// paths, prompts, or transcript content.
333	//
334	// A commit is part of the event's identity, not an incidental trigger, which is
335	// why it is named for one. FilesCommitted and PriorAIHistory are commit-scoped:
336	// the former counts that commit's files, the latter asks whether commits
337	// *before* this one already touched them. UsedSearch is deliberately
338	// SESSION-scoped — the metric asks whether the session EVER consulted search
339	// before landing this commit, so one search early in a session rightly covers
340	// its later commits. The condensation paths that run without a commit (doctor
341	// repair, session-end leftovers) deliberately emit nothing — see
342	// newCommitCondensedSignal for why folding them in would corrupt the
343	// denominator rather than complete it.
344	type CommitCondensedSignal struct {
345		// Agent is the session-owning agent's registry key (e.g. "claude-code"),
346		// matching the agent property on skill and command events.
347		Agent string
348		// UsedSearch reports whether the session invoked `entire search`. Nil means
349		// the question was not answerable for this agent's transcript format, and
350		// the property is then OMITTED from the payload rather than sent as false —
351		// so a consumer filtering on `used_search = false` excludes unknowns instead
352		// of silently counting them as "did not search". UsedSearchSource always

354		UsedSearch *bool
355		// UsedSearchSource records how UsedSearch was determined: "unsupported",
356		// "none", "command", or "subagent". Always present.
357		UsedSearchSource string
358		// PriorAIHistory reports whether any committed file was touched by a
359		// recent AI checkpoint commit before this one. Nil means the git-log probe
360		// could not run (git unavailable, cancelled ctx, shallow-clone failure) and
361		// the property is then OMITTED from the payload rather than sent as false —
362		// same rationale as UsedSearch: a fabricated "no prior history" deflates
363		// the very miss rate this event exists to measure. A commit that landed no
364		// files is a measured false, not an omission.

366		// FilesCommitted is the number of files this checkpoint touched.

396		// UsedSearch and PriorAIHistory.

399		}

402		}

413	// signal. Like TrackPluginDetached, it only honors the env opt-out itself —

430	// SendEvents processes one or more event payloads in the detached subprocess.
431	// This is called by the hidden __send_analytics command.
432	//
433	// The argv carries either a single event object or an array of them; both
434	// shapes are accepted. Leniency matters beyond convenience: the child is
435	// re-executed from os.Executable(), so a self-update that replaces the binary
436	// between spawn and exec can hand a payload to a build other than the one that
437	// wrote it.
438	func SendEvents(payloadJSON string) {
439		payloads := decodeEventPayloads(payloadJSON)
440		if len(payloads) == 0 {
441			return
442		}
443	
444		// Create PostHog client - no need for fast timeouts since we're detached
445		// Read API key and endpoint from package-level vars (not passed via argv for security)
446		client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(PostHogAPIKey, posthog.Config{
447			Endpoint:     PostHogEndpoint,
448			Logger:       silentLogger{},
449			DisableGeoIP: posthog.Ptr(true),
450		})
451		if err != nil {
452			return
453		}
454		defer func() {
455			_ = client.Close()
456		}()
457	
458		// Resolve the installed git version best-effort, once for the whole batch.
459		// A missing or failing git must never block the rest of the telemetry — the
460		// property is simply omitted when it can't be determined.
461		gitVer := gitVersion(context.Background())
462	
463		for _, payload := range payloads {
464			props := posthog.NewProperties()
465			for k, v := range payload.Properties {
466				props.Set(k, v)
467			}
468			if gitVer != "" {
469				props.Set("git_version", gitVer)
470			}
471	
472			//nolint:errcheck // Best effort telemetry - don't block on result
473			_ = client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
474				DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
475				Event:      payload.Event,
476				Properties: props,
477				Timestamp:  payload.Timestamp,
478			})
479		}
480	}
481	
482	// decodeEventPayloads parses the argv payload as either an array of events or a
483	// single event. Malformed input yields no payloads: telemetry is best-effort and
484	// the detached child has nowhere to report a parse failure.
485	func decodeEventPayloads(payloadJSON string) []EventPayload {
486		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(payloadJSON)
487		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[") {
488			var batch []EventPayload
489			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), &batch); err != nil {
490				return nil
491			}
492			return batch
493		}
494		var single EventPayload
495		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), &single); err != nil {
496			return nil
497		}
498		return []EventPayload{single}
499	}
500	
501	// gitVersion returns the installed git version (e.g. "2.43.0"), best-effort.
502	// It returns "" when git is absent, the command fails or times out, or the
503	// output cannot be parsed — callers must treat "" as "unknown" and move on.
504	func gitVersion(ctx context.Context) string {
505		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
506		defer cancel()
507	
508		out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "--version").Output()
509		if err != nil {
510			return ""
511		}
512		return parseGitVersion(string(out))
513	}
514	
515	// parseGitVersion extracts the version token from `git --version` output, which
516	// looks like "git version 2.43.0" (sometimes with a platform suffix such as
517	// "git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)"). Returns "" if the shape is unexpected.
518	func parseGitVersion(out string) string {
519		fields := strings.Fields(out)
520		if len(fields) < 3 || fields[0] != "git" || fields[1] != "version" {
521			return ""
522		}
523		return fields[2]
524	}

368		repoFilters     []string

377	// extractInlineRepoFilters extracts only repo: prefixed filters from a query
378	// string, returning the remaining query text and the list of repo values.
379	// Unlike search.ParseSearchInput, this does NOT consume author:, date:, or
380	// branch: tokens — those are checkpoint-search-only and should be treated as
381	// literal text in code search queries.
382	func extractInlineRepoFilters(query string) (remaining string, repos []string) {
383		var kept []string
384		for _, part := range strings.Fields(query) {
385			if strings.HasPrefix(part, "repo:") {
386				// Split comma-separated values (repo:a,b → [a, b]), matching
387				// checkpoint search's parseListFilter behavior. Trim quotes so
388				// repo:"gh/owner/repo" works like the unquoted form.
389				for _, v := range strings.Split(part[5:], ",") {
390					v = strings.Trim(v, `"'`)
391					if v != "" {
392						repos = append(repos, v)
393					}
394				}
395			} else {
396				kept = append(kept, part)
397			}
398		}
399		return strings.Join(kept, " "), repos
400	}

458	// plane, group by cell/jurisdiction, search each cell in parallel, merge.

489	// searchAllCells fans out code search across all cells that host the user's
490	// repos, using the shared cell-routing foundation (cell_fanout.go):
491	//  1. List repos from the control plane (entire-core) to discover cells
492	//  2. Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs
493	//  3. Group by cell and resolve baseURLs via the shared helpers
494	//  4. Fan out via fanOutCells with per-cell codesearch.Search calls
495	//  5. Merge results (sorted by score, capped to limit)
496	func searchAllCells(ctx context.Context, opts codeSearchOpts) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
497		// Step 1: Get repos index from the control plane. *coreapi.Client
498		// satisfies cellCoreClient (passed to resolveCellBaseURLs below as such).
499		coreClient, err := coreapi.New()
500		if err != nil {
501			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
502				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
503			}
504			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving control-plane client: %w", err)
505		}
506	
507		reposCtx, reposCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
508		defer reposCancel()
509	
510		repoIndex, err := coreClient.ListRepos(reposCtx, coreapi.ListReposParams{})
511		if err != nil {
512			return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing repos for cell discovery: %w", err)
513		}
514	
515		if repoIndex.Truncated {
516			logging.Warn(ctx, "repo index truncated; code search results may be incomplete")
517		}
518	
519		// Step 2: Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs and narrow to matching cells.
520		indexRepos := repoIndex.Repos
521		if len(opts.repoFilters) > 0 {
522			resolved, filtered := resolveRepoFilters(opts.repoFilters, repoIndex.Repos)
523			if len(resolved) == 0 {
524				hint := ""
525				if repoIndex.Truncated {
526					hint = " (repo index was truncated — the repo may exist but was not included)"
527				}
528				return nil, fmt.Errorf("no matching repositories found for filter %q%s", opts.repoFilters, hint)
529			}
530			opts.resolvedRepoIDs = resolved
531			indexRepos = filtered
532		}
533	
534		// Step 3: Group repos by cell and resolve baseURLs via shared helpers.
535		// Routes by routedRepoPlacement like semantic search (see its doc). The
536		// CLI is deliberately ahead of the BFF's code-search.ts here, which stays
537		// canonical until its code-read chain (/symbols, /usages, file viewer)
538		// flips with it — identical behavior until then, and core electing
539		// divergent primaries is gated on that web flip (tracked on ENT-1776).
540		pinned := len(opts.repoFilters) > 0
541		cells, skippedRepos := groupReposByCell(indexRepos)
542		skippedRepos = reportableSkippedRepos(ctx, pinned, len(cells), skippedRepos)
543		if len(cells) == 0 {
544			return &codesearch.SearchResponse{SkippedRepos: skippedRepos}, nil
545		}
546		resolveCellBaseURLs(ctx, coreClient, cells)
547	
548		// Step 4: Fan out via the shared fanOutCells helper.
549		// Each cell gets the full limit for single-cell, or 2x for multi-cell so
550		// the merge sees enough candidates from every region for proper global
551		// ranking. mergeSearchResults applies the final cap.
552		perCellLimit := opts.limit
553		if len(cells) > 1 && perCellLimit > 0 {
554			perCellLimit *= 2
555		}
556		results, err := fanOutCells(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, codeSearchCellTimeout, cells, func(ctx context.Context, group cellGroup, client *api.Client) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
557			var repoIDs []string
558			if len(opts.resolvedRepoIDs) > 0 {
559				repoIDs = group.repoIDs
560			}
561			req := codesearch.SearchRequest{
562				Query:         opts.query,
563				Repos:         repoIDs,
564				CaseSensitive: opts.caseSensitive,
565			}
566			if perCellLimit > 0 {
567				req.MaxResults = perCellLimit
568			}
569			return codesearch.Search(ctx, client, req)
570		})
571		if err != nil {
572			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
573				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
574			}
575			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search: %w", err)
576		}
577	
578		merged, err := mergeSearchResults(ctx, opts.limit, results)
579		if err != nil {
580			return nil, err
581		}
582		merged.SkippedRepos = skippedRepos
583		return merged, nil
584	}

586	// resolveRepoFilters matches user-provided filters against the repo index,
587	// returning the ULID list for peregrine and the subset of index entries whose
588	// repos matched (for cell grouping).
589	//
590	// Matching mirrors the BFF (code-search.ts lines 315-319):
591	//
592	//	slug = filter starts with "gh/" ? strip prefix : filter unchanged
593	//	match = id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
594	//
595	// Accepted filter formats:
596	//   - ULID            — matched directly on repo ID (raw filter)
597	//   - gh/owner/repo   — GitHub repo, stripped to owner/repo for FullName match
598	//   - owner/repo      — bare slug, matched on FullName directly
599	func resolveRepoFilters(filters []string, repos []coreapi.RepoIndexEntry) (repoIDs []string, matched []coreapi.RepoIndexEntry) {
600		byName := make(map[string]coreapi.RepoIndexEntry, len(repos))
601		byID := make(map[string]coreapi.RepoIndexEntry, len(repos))
602		for _, r := range repos {
603			byName[strings.ToLower(r.FullName)] = r
604			byID[r.ID] = r
605		}
606		seen := make(map[string]bool) // dedup by ID
607		for _, f := range filters {
608			// BFF only strips gh/ prefix; other prefixes are left as-is.
609			slug := f
610			if strings.HasPrefix(f, "gh/") {
611				slug = f[3:]
612			}
613	
614			// Match order mirrors the BFF: id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
615			// FullName comparison is case-insensitive so casing differences between
616			// the git remote (e.g. entireio/CLI) and the repo index (entireio/cli)
617			// don't cause a "no matching repositories found" failure.
618			var r coreapi.RepoIndexEntry
619			var ok bool
620			if r, ok = byID[f]; !ok {
621				if r, ok = byName[strings.ToLower(slug)]; !ok {
622					r, ok = byName[strings.ToLower(f)]
623				}
624			}
625			if ok && !seen[r.ID] {
626				repoIDs = append(repoIDs, r.ID)
627				matched = append(matched, r)
628				seen[r.ID] = true

634	// mergeSearchResults merges responses from multiple cells into one, combining
635	// results, stats, and repo_stats. Results are sorted by Score (descending) for
636	// global relevance ranking and truncated to limit. Individual cell errors are
637	// logged and skipped, but if ALL cells fail the error is surfaced.
638	func mergeSearchResults(ctx context.Context, limit int, results []cellCallResult[*codesearch.SearchResponse]) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
639		merged := &codesearch.SearchResponse{}
640		var lastErr error
641		successCount := 0
642		for _, r := range results {
643			if r.err != nil {
644				lastErr = r.err
645				continue
646			}
647			if r.value == nil {
648				continue
649			}
650			successCount++
651			merged.Results = append(merged.Results, r.value.Results...)
652			merged.RepoStats = append(merged.RepoStats, r.value.RepoStats...)
653			merged.Stats.TotalMatches += r.value.Stats.TotalMatches
654			merged.Stats.TotalFiles += r.value.Stats.TotalFiles
655			merged.Stats.ReposSearched += r.value.Stats.ReposSearched
656			if r.value.Stats.DurationMs > merged.Stats.DurationMs {
657				merged.Stats.DurationMs = r.value.Stats.DurationMs // wall-clock = slowest cell
658			}
659			if merged.Query == "" {
660				merged.Query = r.value.Query
661			}
662		}
663	
664		if successCount == 0 && lastErr != nil {
665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search failed: %w", lastErr)
666		}
667	
668		// Track partial failures so consumers (especially --json) can see them.
669		var failedJurisdictions []string
670		for _, r := range results {
671			if r.err == nil {
672				continue
673			}
674			failedJurisdictions = append(failedJurisdictions, r.group.label())
675		}
676		if len(failedJurisdictions) > 0 {
677			logging.Warn(ctx, "code search partial failure; results may be incomplete",
678				"succeeded", successCount,
679				"total", len(results),
680				"failed_cells", failedJurisdictions)
681		}
682	
683		// Sort by score descending so results are globally ranked by relevance,
684		// not grouped by whichever cell returned first. Stable sort with a
685		// tiebreaker keeps --json output deterministic across runs.
686		sort.SliceStable(merged.Results, func(i, j int) bool {
687			a, b := merged.Results[i], merged.Results[j]
688			if a.Score != b.Score {
689				return a.Score > b.Score
690			}
691			if a.Repo != b.Repo {
692				return a.Repo < b.Repo
693			}
694			if a.Path != b.Path {
695				return a.Path < b.Path
696			}
697			return a.Line < b.Line
698		})
699	
700		// Deduplicate results that may appear from overlapping cells (e.g. a repo
701		// with empty jurisdiction searched via both home and explicit cell).
702		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(merged.Results))
703		deduped := merged.Results[:0]
704		for _, r := range merged.Results {
705			key := r.Repo + "\x00" + r.Path + "\x00" + fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", r.Line, r.Column)
706			if seen[key] {
707				continue
708			}
709			seen[key] = true
710			deduped = append(deduped, r)
711		}
712		merged.Results = deduped
713	
714		// Deduplicate RepoStats by repo name. The fan-out routes each repo to one
715		// canonical cell (ENT-1672), so a repo appearing in more than one cell
716		// response should no longer happen via placements — this remains as a
717		// guard for overlapping cell scopes (e.g. a repo with empty jurisdiction
718		// searched via both home and explicit cell) returning the SAME content,
719		// not additional matches. Keep one representative
720		// entry per repo (the max of each count; mirror copies are identical, max
721		// only guards against minor per-cell skew) instead of summing, and record
722		// the duplicated portion so the aggregate stats can drop the double-count.
723		type repoStatAcc struct {
724			idx                    int
725			sumMatches, maxMatches int
726			sumFiles, maxFiles     int
727			cellCount              int
728		}
729		accByRepo := make(map[string]*repoStatAcc, len(merged.RepoStats))
730		var dedupedStats []codesearch.RepoStats
731		for _, rs := range merged.RepoStats {
732			acc, ok := accByRepo[rs.Repo]
733			if !ok {
734				acc = &repoStatAcc{idx: len(dedupedStats)}
735				accByRepo[rs.Repo] = acc
736				dedupedStats = append(dedupedStats, codesearch.RepoStats{Repo: rs.Repo})
737			}
738			acc.cellCount++
739			acc.sumMatches += rs.MatchCount
740			acc.sumFiles += rs.FileCount
741			acc.maxMatches = max(acc.maxMatches, rs.MatchCount)
742			acc.maxFiles = max(acc.maxFiles, rs.FileCount)
743		}
744		var overcountMatches, overcountFiles, overcountRepos int
745		for _, acc := range accByRepo {
746			dedupedStats[acc.idx].MatchCount = acc.maxMatches
747			dedupedStats[acc.idx].FileCount = acc.maxFiles
748			overcountMatches += acc.sumMatches - acc.maxMatches
749			overcountFiles += acc.sumFiles - acc.maxFiles
750			overcountRepos += acc.cellCount - 1
751		}
752		merged.RepoStats = dedupedStats
753	
754		// The per-cell Stats were summed above, so a repo answered by more than
755		// one cell was counted once per cell. Subtract the duplicated copies
756		// identified via RepoStats so the totals reflect distinct content, not
757		// the same content seen twice. This preserves per-cell truncation (the
758		// base is peregrine's own totals; we only remove the provable duplicate
759		// portion) and zero-match repos (they contribute 0 to the subtraction).
760		// A repo with matches but no RepoStats row, or a zero-match mirror repo,
761		// can't be de-duplicated from the response and keeps its summed
762		// contribution — a mild over-count, far less misleading than reporting
763		// every mirrored match twice. Clamp at zero against inconsistent input.
764		merged.Stats.TotalMatches = max(0, merged.Stats.TotalMatches-overcountMatches)
765		merged.Stats.TotalFiles = max(0, merged.Stats.TotalFiles-overcountFiles)
766		merged.Stats.ReposSearched = max(0, merged.Stats.ReposSearched-overcountRepos)
767	
768		// Cap to the caller's requested limit.
769		if limit > 0 && len(merged.Results) > limit {
770			merged.Results = merged.Results[:limit]
771		}
772	
773		// Surface partial failures in the response so JSON consumers can detect them.
774		merged.FailedJurisdictions = failedJurisdictions
775	
776		return merged, nil
777	}

823	// writeCodeSearchText renders code search results grouped by file (ripgrep
824	// style): a colored "repo:path" header per file, indented line-numbered
825	// matches beneath it, and a dimmed stats footer. Colors are applied only when
826	// the writer supports them (styles.colorEnabled); piped output stays plain.
827	func writeCodeSearchText(w io.Writer, resp *codesearch.SearchResponse, styles statusStyles, caseSensitive bool) {
828		if len(resp.Results) == 0 {
829			// Both causes can hold at once; reporting only the first leaves the
830			// user to discover the other from a bare result count.
831			var causes []string
832			if len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 {
833				causes = append(causes, "some regions failed: "+strings.Join(resp.FailedJurisdictions, ", "))
834			}
835			if len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0 {
836				causes = append(causes, "skipped repos with no searchable placement: "+strings.Join(resp.SkippedRepos, ", "))
837			}
838			if len(causes) > 0 {
839				fmt.Fprintf(w, "No code search results found (%s)\n", strings.Join(causes, "; "))
840			} else {
841				fmt.Fprintln(w, "No code search results found.")
842			}
843			return
844		}
845	
846		// Group results by repo:path, preserving first-appearance order so the
847		// best-scored file stays on top (results arrive globally score-sorted).
848		type fileGroup struct {
849			key     string
850			results []codesearch.Result
851		}
852		var groups []fileGroup
853		idx := make(map[string]int, len(resp.Results))
854		for _, r := range resp.Results {
855			key := r.Repo + ":" + r.Path
856			i, ok := idx[key]
857			if !ok {
858				i = len(groups)
859				idx[key] = i
860				groups = append(groups, fileGroup{key: key})
861			}
862			groups[i].results = append(groups[i].results, r)
863		}
864	
865		shown := 0
866		for gi, g := range groups {
867			if gi == maxCodeSearchFiles {
868				break
869			}
870			fmt.Fprintln(w)
871			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.cyan, g.key))
872			for mi, r := range g.results {
873				if mi == maxCodeSearchFileMatches {
874					break
875				}
876				// Truncate before highlighting but append the ellipsis after,
877				// so the non-ASCII "…" doesn't disable case-insensitive
878				// highlighting (isASCII) for the rest of the line.
879				line := r.ContextLine
880				ellipsis := ""
881				if runes := []rune(line); len(runes) > maxContextLineLen {
882					line = string(runes[:maxContextLineLen])
883					ellipsis = "…"
884				}
885				lineNo := styles.render(styles.dim, fmt.Sprintf("%d:", r.Line))
886				fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s%s\n", lineNo, highlightCodeMatches(line, resp.Query, styles, caseSensitive), ellipsis)
887				shown++
888			}
889			// ponytail: overflow counts only what this page fetched (peregrine
890			// has no per-file totals); a hot file shows "+ 97 matches" at most.
891			if extra := len(g.results) - maxCodeSearchFileMatches; extra > 0 {
892				label := "matches"
893				if extra == 1 {
894					label = "match"
895				}
896				fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.dim, fmt.Sprintf("  + %d %s", extra, label)))
897			}
898		}
899	
900		var summary string
901		if resp.Stats.TotalMatches > shown {
902			summary = fmt.Sprintf("Showing %d of %d matches across %d files in %d repos (%.0fms)",
903				shown, resp.Stats.TotalMatches, resp.Stats.TotalFiles, resp.Stats.ReposSearched, resp.Stats.DurationMs)
904		} else {
905			summary = fmt.Sprintf("%d matches across %d files in %d repos (%.0fms)",
906				resp.Stats.TotalMatches, resp.Stats.TotalFiles, resp.Stats.ReposSearched, resp.Stats.DurationMs)
907		}
908		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n%s\n", styles.render(styles.dim, summary))
909		if len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 {
910			warning := fmt.Sprintf("Warning: results may be incomplete (failed jurisdictions: %s)",
911				strings.Join(resp.FailedJurisdictions, ", "))
912			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.yellow, warning))
913		}
914		if len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0 {
915			warning := "Warning: skipped repo(s) with no searchable placement (missing or not ready): " + strings.Join(resp.SkippedRepos, ", ")
916			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.yellow, warning))
917		}
918	}

920	// highlightCodeMatches bold-red highlights occurrences of query in line
921	// (grep convention). Matching mirrors the search: case-insensitive unless
922	// caseSensitive is set. Case folding is only applied when both strings are
923	// pure ASCII, since Unicode case mappings can change byte widths and
924	// misalign offsets against the original line; non-ASCII input falls back to
925	// exact matching. Returns line unchanged when color is disabled or there's
926	// nothing to highlight.
927	func highlightCodeMatches(line, query string, styles statusStyles, caseSensitive bool) string {
928		if !styles.colorEnabled || query == "" {
929			return line
930		}
931		haystack, needle := line, query
932		if !caseSensitive && isASCII(line) && isASCII(query) {
933			haystack, needle = strings.ToLower(line), strings.ToLower(query)
934		}
935		matchStyle := styles.red.Bold(true)
936		var b strings.Builder
937		i := 0
938		for {
939			j := strings.Index(haystack[i:], needle)
940			if j < 0 {
941				break
942			}
943			j += i
944			b.WriteString(line[i:j])
945			b.WriteString(matchStyle.Render(line[j : j+len(needle)]))
946			i = j + len(needle)
947		}
948		if i == 0 {
949			return line // no matches; skip the builder copy
950		}
951		b.WriteString(line[i:])
952		return b.String()
953	}

955	// isASCII reports whether s contains only ASCII bytes.
956	func isASCII(s string) bool {
957		for i := range len(s) {
958			if s[i] >= utf8.RuneSelf {
959				return false
960			}
961		}
962		return true
963	}

965	// paginateSearchResults slices results for the requested client-side page,
966	// normalizing limit and page, and returns the page slice (never nil) plus the
967	// normalized pagination values.
968	func paginateSearchResults(results []search.Result, limit, page int) (pageResults []search.Result, total, totalPages, normLimit, normPage int) {
969		if limit <= 0 {
970			limit = resultsPerPage
971		}
972		total = len(results)
973		totalPages = (total + limit - 1) / limit
974		if totalPages < 1 {
975			totalPages = 1
976		}
977		if page < 1 {
978			page = 1
979		}
980		start := (page - 1) * limit
981		end := start + limit
982		if start < total {
983			if end > total {
984				end = total
985			}
986			pageResults = results[start:end]
987		}
988		if pageResults == nil {
989			pageResults = []search.Result{}
990		}
991		return pageResults, total, totalPages, limit, page
992	}

1075			return ""
1076		}
1077		return snippet
